questions.explanation: The trap claim is: The alarm is on whenever A is on, because OR works just like AND. In fact Read the circuit gate by gate: the alarm is on only when (A AND B) are both 1 or NOT C is 1 - that is, when A and B are both on, or C is off (or both). The AND output and NOT C are worked out first, and only their OR result drives the alarm.
